inline_comments.comment: The body text says "In Storybook 9, on-device addons...must be listed under the `deviceAddons` key" but this section is headed "From version 10.3.0 to 10.4.0". These are contradictory — readers don't know whether the behavior changed in v9 or v10.4. The prose should reference the version that matches the section heading (e.g., "In Storybook 10.4").

`rnOndeviceAddonsToDeviceAddons` is placed **before** `rnstorybookConfig` in `allFixes`, but the PR description says "immediately after `rnstorybookConfig`". `rnstorybookConfig` renames the config directory from `.storybook` to `.rnstorybook`. If that migration hasn't run yet (first-time run on a pre-migration project), the `mainConfigPath` handed to `rnOndeviceAddonsToDeviceAddons.run` could still point to the old `.storybook/main.ts`, causing the write to land in the wrong file. This should run after `rnstorybookConfig`.

The test description "handles the case where @storybook/react-native is in dependencies (not devDependencies)" implies a distinct code path for regular `dependencies` vs `devDependencies`. However, `packageManager.getAllDependencies()` already merges both sets, so there is no separate branch exercised here. Either rename this test to describe what it actually verifies (a successful detection with a version range), or remove it as a duplicate of the preceding success test.

The `prompt` function ignores the `result` parameter, so the message gives no indication of *which* addons will be moved. Compare how other fixes (e.g. `rnstorybookConfig`) include specific values in their prompts. Consider listing the affected addon names (from `result.ondeviceAddons`) so users know exactly what will change before confirming.

general_comments.comment: The unrelated test-import cleanup changes (adding `.ts` extensions and reformatting multi-line call arguments in the four `REACT_NATIVE` test files) are bundled into this PR. While harmless, mixing unrelated refactors makes it harder to bisect or revert the feature change in isolation. These should ideally be separate commits or a separate PR.
